sources.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge Part II lecture notes, 2004/05; author-hosted PDF)
sources.locator: Chapter 3 §§3.1-3.6, printed pp. 46-73 (PDF pp. 52-79): §3.1.1 angular velocity Eqs. (3.3)-(3.10); §3.2 inertia tensor Eqs. (3.17)-(3.23); §3.2.2 angular momentum Eqs. (3.27)-(3.28); §3.3 Euler equations Eqs. (3.31)-(3.33); §3.4.3 asymmetric-top stability Eqs. (3.40)-(3.45); §3.5 Euler angles Eq. (3.54) and §3.5.2 Eqs. (3.55)-(3.58); §3.6 heavy top Eqs. (3.62)-(3.70)

contents.name: §3.1.1 Angular velocity, Eqs. (3.5)-(3.10): antisymmetry of the body-frame rate matrix and the single-index vector omega
contents.support: The item proves the differentiated orthogonality relation for a curve in SO(3) and the sum/transpose/product rules used to obtain it.

contents.name: §3.1 angular velocity as a vector acting by cross product, Eqs. (3.6)-(3.9)
contents.support: The item reconstructs the skew-matrix/vector bijection, proves [omega]_x z=omega x z, and adds the conjugation law.

contents.name: §3.1 rigid placement as overall translation plus rotation, Eqs. (3.3)-(3.4)
contents.support: The definition records x(t,rho)=c(t)+R(t)rho, the body angular velocity and material velocities with an explicit SO(3) convention.

contents.name: §3.2 inertia tensor for discrete and continuous bodies, Eqs. (3.17)-(3.20)
contents.support: The measure-theoretic definition generalizes the source's sums and density integrals to arbitrary bounded finite Borel measures.

contents.name: §3.2 symmetry and positivity of the inertia tensor, Eq. (3.22), with the equality case (all mass on a line)
contents.support: The item proves symmetry, the quadratic identity, and the exact criterion: zero quadratic form in omega means zero mass off R omega; positive definiteness means positive mass off every line through the origin.

contents.name: §3.2 principal axes by orthogonal diagonalization, Eq. (3.21) and following text
contents.support: The corollary derives an orthonormal eigenbasis, I_j=0 iff the entire mass lies on R e_j, and positivity/invertibility when no line carries the entire mass.

contents.name: §3.2.2 angular momentum L=I omega, Eqs. (3.27)-(3.28), and the centre-of-mass kinetic split, Eq. (3.30)
contents.support: The theorem integrates the pointwise identities over the measure and proves K=1/2 m|c'|^2+1/2 omega^T I omega and L_c=R I omega.

contents.name: §3.3 Euler's equations in principal axes, with and without torque, Eqs. (3.31)-(3.33)
contents.support: The theorem derives I omega'+omega x I omega=R^T tau from an explicitly adopted balance hypothesis and records the torque-free invariants.

contents.name: §3.4.3 asymmetric-top perturbation equations and sign criterion, Eqs. (3.41)-(3.45)
contents.support: The theorem proves the linearization and the oscillatory/exponential dichotomy with explicit formulas and identified hypotheses.

contents.name: §3.4.3 stability about the largest and smallest moments
contents.support: The item gives a complete nonlinear argument via the invariants and compact continuation, which the source indicates only through the linear sign criterion.

contents.name: §3.4.3 instability of the intermediate axis
contents.support: The item exhibits an explicit invariant branch with l_1'>=c_0 l_1>0 and a logarithmic escape-time bound.

contents.name: §3.4.1 The symmetric top, Eqs. (3.34)-(3.37), and §3.5.3 free-symmetric-top precession, Eqs. (3.59)-(3.60)
contents.reason: The repeated-moment case I_1=I_2 has a different equilibrium set and is not covered by the distinct-moment stability and linearization claims of this page; no symmetric-top assertion is made here.

contents.name: §3.4.2 Example: the Earth's wobble; §3.6.4 precession of the equinoxes
contents.reason: These are astronomical and observational discussions; the page makes no empirical or measured claim and reproduces no numerical anecdote.

contents.name: §3.4.4 Poinsot construction of free rigid-body motion
contents.reason: The geometric polhode/herpolhode construction is not among the claims of this pair and no equivalent invariant-set geometry is asserted.

contents.name: §3.5 the three ordered rotations and the Euler-angle parametrization, Eq. (3.54)
contents.support: The lemma proves R_z,R_y in SO(3), their composition law and their derivatives, which the source states without proof.

contents.name: §3.5.2 angular velocity in Euler angles, Eqs. (3.55)-(3.58)
contents.support: The lemma recomputes the body angular velocity for the displayed convention and proves the components and squared transverse sum.

contents.name: §3.6 heavy symmetric top: Lagrangian, cyclic momenta, reduced energy, Eqs. (3.62)-(3.70)
contents.support: The theorem derives the conserved a,b, the explicit rates, the conserved reduced energy and the theta equation from the displayed system.

contents.name: §3.6.1 letting the top go and §3.6.2 uniform precession
contents.support: The example verifies a constant-rate precession against every reduction clause, including the vanishing of U'.

contents.name: §3.6.3 sleeping-top threshold
contents.reason: The upright threshold lies at the chart boundary theta=0, excluded from the Euler-angle domain; no threshold claim is made on this page.

contents.name: §3.7 Motion of deformable bodies
contents.reason: Deformable-body kinematics belongs to the continuum pair of this run, not to this rigid-body pair.

sources.title: K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics (Stony Brook; merged author PDF)
sources.locator: Chapter 4 'Rigid Body Motion' §§4.1-4.7 (chapter pages 1-25 of 32; merged-volume printed pp. 55-79): §4.1 Eqs. (4.1)-(4.10); §4.2 Eqs. (4.16)-(4.28); §4.3 fixed-axis and rolling; §4.4 Eqs. (4.61)-(4.69); §4.5 Eqs. (4.70)-(4.90); §4.6 moving frames; §4.7 exercises

contents.name: §4.1 rigidity and six degrees of freedom; moving basis, skew rate matrix, transport theorem, Eqs. (4.1)-(4.10)
contents.support: The definition restates the moving-frame angular velocity and material-velocity relation with an explicit SO(3) convention.

contents.name: §4.2 rotational kinetic energy through the inertia tensor, Eqs. (4.14)-(4.16)
contents.support: The theorem proves the kinetic-energy formula for a centred measure-theoretic mass distribution, including the translation-rotation split.

contents.name: §4.2 inertia tensor as a symmetric second-moment matrix, Eq. (4.16)
contents.support: The definition generalizes the source's continuous integral to bounded finite Borel measures and fixes all conventions componentwise.

contents.name: §4.2 angular momentum L=I omega, Eq. (4.22)
contents.support: The item proves L_c=R I omega, the body-frame statement of the source.

contents.name: §4.2 principal axes
contents.support: The corollary derives an orthonormal eigenbasis, I_j=0 iff the entire mass lies on R e_j, and positivity/invertibility when no line carries the entire mass.

contents.name: §4.2 parallel-axis relation, Eq. (4.28)
contents.reason: The translation rule for the inertia tensor is a separate computation placed with the verification examples of a later mathematics pair, not on this page.

contents.name: §4.3 fixed-axis rotation and rolling constraints
contents.reason: Fixed-axis and rolling constraints belong to the constraint pair; this page claims no constraint reduction.

contents.name: §4.4 free symmetric top and Euler equations, Eqs. (4.61)-(4.69)
contents.support: The Euler-equation content is proved from the adopted balance hypothesis; the Poinsot and symmetric-top discussions are not reproduced.

contents.name: §4.4 intermediate-axis stability left to the reader as an exercise
contents.support: The item supplies a complete independent argument with an escape-time bound; nothing rests on the unworked exercise.

contents.name: §4.5 Euler angles and principal-axis angular-velocity components, Eq. (4.74)
contents.support: The lemma recomputes the components for the convention displayed on this page and proves the norm identity.

contents.name: §4.5 exact reduced effective potential, Eq. (4.82)
contents.support: The reduced energy and theta equation are proved from the displayed system.

contents.name: §4.5 fast-top approximation and upright threshold, Eqs. (4.83)-(4.85)
contents.reason: The fast-spin approximation and the threshold at theta=0 are not among the claims made here.

contents.name: §4.6 motion in accelerating frames and canonical versus kinetic momentum
contents.reason: Moving-frame acceleration and canonical momentum belong to the geometry and variations pairs of the same run.

contents.name: §4.7 the thirty-seven chapter exercises
contents.reason: Exercises were surveyed but are not used as suppliers; no exercise solution is cited.

sources.title: G. J. Sussman and J. Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, 2nd ed. (MIT Press, 2014), official publisher archive; complete text extracted locally at research/first-principles-2026-10-03/non-relativistic-classical-mechanics/reader-sicm/text/chapter002.txt

contents.name: §2.1 Rotational kinetic energy and the centre-of-mass split, Eqs. (2.8)-(2.10)
contents.support: The theorem proves the translation-rotation split for the measure-theoretic placement.

contents.name: §2.2 Kinematics of rotation: orientation path, skew angular-velocity matrix, body components, Eqs. (2.14)-(2.30)
contents.support: The definition fixes the convention R^T R'=[omega]_x, matching the source's DM M^T and M^T omega.

contents.name: §2.3 Moments of inertia and §2.4 the inertia tensor, Eq. (2.41)
contents.support: The item proves symmetry, the quadratic identity, and the exact criterion: zero quadratic form in omega means zero mass off R omega; positive definiteness means positive mass off every line through the origin.

contents.name: §2.5 Principal moments of inertia and the diagonal form
contents.support: The corollary derives an orthonormal eigenbasis, I_j=0 iff the entire mass lies on R e_j, and positivity/invertibility when no line carries the entire mass.

contents.name: §2.6 Vector angular momentum, Eq. (2.51)
contents.support: The item proves L_c=R I omega by integrating the pointwise cross-product identity.

contents.name: §2.7 Euler angles and the coordinate rotation matrices
contents.support: The parametrization and coordinate rotation matrices are defined with their derivative identities proved locally.

contents.name: §2.8.2 qualitative features of free rigid-body motion: energy and angular-momentum level curves, intermediate-axis behaviour
contents.support: The invariant-level-set picture is absorbed into the stability and instability arguments, which use the two conserved quantities and an explicit branch.

contents.name: §2.8.1 numerically computing the motion of free rigid bodies
contents.reason: The chapter's computational integration and error plots are not used; this page contains no numerical integration result.

contents.name: §2.9 Euler's equations in principal components, Eqs. (2.80)-(2.83)
contents.support: The theorem proves the component equations and the conservation of the two invariants.

contents.name: §2.10 axisymmetric tops: Lagrangian and reduced energy, Eqs. (2.84)-(2.91)
contents.support: The reduction theorem derives the conserved momenta, explicit rates, reduced energy and theta equation.

contents.name: §2.11 potential in an external field and the simplified lunar spin-orbit model
contents.reason: Multipole expansions and the simplified spin-orbit model are not claimed here and carry observational qualifications.

contents.name: §2.12 quaternions and Eq. (2.133)
contents.reason: Quaternion reconstruction of orientation belongs to the rotation double-cover pair of this run.

contents.name: §3.4.3 perturbation equations and their sign criterion, Eqs. (3.42)-(3.45)

contents.name: §3.6.2 uniform precession of the heavy top

contents.name: §3.2 inertia-tensor computations for point-mass systems, Eqs. (3.19)-(3.23)
contents.support: The example recomputes three finite point-mass inertia matrices and checks them against the positivity criterion.

contents.name: §4.2 inertia-tensor components of discrete mass distributions

contents.name: §4.4 principal-axis rotation stability

contents.name: §4.5 reduced potential and precession of the symmetric top
